headline: GOLD, SILVER POST WORST WEEK IN 8 MONTHS — Spot Closes at $3,543 as Liquidity Crunch Deepens; Analysts Split on Whether Bottom Is Near
snippet: Gold spot closed the week at approximately $3,543.60 — down 8.71% for the week and touching a Friday intraday low of $3,502.93 — while silver posted a 14-15% weekly decline, as Kitco's November 20 report documented the worst weekly performance for both metals since March 2026, driven by a deepening liquidity crunch in which forced selling from leveraged AI-linked equities spilled over into precious metals, breaking the traditional safe-haven correlation. Analysts cited a simultaneously rising US dollar, persistent Fed rate-hike expectations, and thin Thanksgiving holiday week trading as the backdrop for further near-term volatility — but TD Securities described the selloff as potentially "gold's saving grace" as prices dropped sharply into oversold territory, with technical analysts eyeing $3,200–$3,450 as the structural support band and a PCE inflation print the week of December 1 as the data catalyst that could either confirm further downside or mark the correction low.

headline: KITCO SURVEY: 60% OF WALL STREET ANALYSTS STAY BEARISH AFTER $3,500 TEST — Thanksgiving Holiday Week Thins Trading; PCE Data Is Next Pivot
snippet: Kitco's November 20 weekly sentiment survey found nine of fifteen professional market participants — 60% — calling for further gold price declines in the coming week, while the remaining six were either bullish or neutral, a bearish skew that reflects the market's rejection of Friday's $3,500 test as a credible bottom. With a shortened trading week ahead due to the US Thanksgiving holiday reducing institutional liquidity on Wednesday through Friday, and PCE inflation data due the week of December 1 representing the next major macro catalyst before the December FOMC meeting, one analyst described the holiday week as "a low-liquidity neutral-to-bearish environment" where thin conditions could amplify any negative data surprise heading into year-end.

headline: HAS SILVER'S BUBBLE FINALLY POPPED? — Silver Lags Gold by 15% in Worst Relative Performance of 2026 as Both Metals Crash
snippet: Kitco's November 18 analysis of silver's relative underperformance against gold — with silver trading near $42-43 per ounce after peaking above $121 in January 2026, a correction exceeding 65% — frames the question of whether the industrial-precious metal hybrid has exhausted its speculative premium and is now converging back toward its traditional gold-ratio range. While silver's supply deficit remains structural at six consecutive years and 762 million ounces cumulative drawdown, the rapid de-rating of AI-infrastructure demand expectations has collapsed the core narrative that drove silver's January blowoff to record highs, and analysts disagree on whether the current $42-43 level represents a sustainable base or whether further technical selling toward the $30-35 range is possible in the event of additional Fed tightening into 2027.

headline: COPPER PHYSICAL MARKET TIGHTENS EVEN AS PRICE CRASHES — China Import Premium Hits $360 as Shanghai Inventory Falls 18% in One Week
snippet: Despite LME copper entering bear market territory near $5.50/lb in the week of November 17-20, 2026, copper's physical market in China told a sharply different story: Shanghai Futures Exchange copper inventories declined 18% in the week to November 14, while import premiums in China hit US$360 per tonne — a level that signals genuine end-user demand tightness rather than speculative buying — creating an unusual divergence between financial market prices and physical availability that ore and smelting constraints at Chinese refineries are struggling to close. For junior mining investors navigating the selloff, the premium spike provides a data-driven argument that the financial conditions-driven copper price rout is severing the connection between commodity prices and underlying supply-demand fundamentals, setting up a potential sharp recovery when the macro headwind from rate expectations reverses.

headline: PHOENIX METALS DRILLS 169M AT 1.30% CuEq IN FIRST LEXINGTON HOLES — New BC Copper-Gold System Emerges in Greenwood District Near Grand Forks
snippet: Phoenix Metals (TSX: PCA) reported on November 18 that the first nine diamond drill holes, totalling 3,063 metres, at its Lexington Target in the Greenwood Copper Gold District near Grand Forks, British Columbia, returned a 169-metre interval grading 1.30% copper equivalent (1.02 g/t Au, 0.22% Cu, 3.8 g/t Ag) — a broad first-hole intersection in a district that produced historical copper-gold VMS and porphyry deposits and has seen renewed major-company interest in recent years. The 169-metre width at a copper-equivalent grade above 1% in the first systematic drilling of the Lexington Target establishes a system of meaningful scale in one of southern BC's under-explored polymetallic corridors, with drilling continuing as the company tests structural controls and depth extensions of the mineralized zone.

headline: IVANHOE ELECTRIC DISCOVERS CU-AU-AG AT GLEESON ARIZONA — Breccia and Carbonate-Hosted System Found Below 1,000m; Two Rigs Active
snippet: Ivanhoe Electric (TSX/NYSE: IE) announced on November 19 that its first drill holes at the Gleeson Copper-Gold Project in southeastern Arizona — adjacent to a historic polymetallic district — intersected breccia and carbonate replacement-hosted copper-gold-silver-zinc mineralization below 1,000 metres depth, confirming the presence of an intrusive-related precious and base metals system distinct from the company's flagship Santa Cruz copper project 100 kilometres to the northwest. With two drill rigs active at Gleeson and Typhoon electromagnetic surveys having identified multiple conductive targets at depth, the discovery adds a new multi-commodity exploration front to Ivanhoe Electric's Arizona portfolio at a time when the company is advancing Santa Cruz toward a construction decision targeting first copper cathode output in 2029.

headline: BUNKER HILL CONSORTIUM WINS EXCLUSIVE KENYA MRIMA HILL RARE EARTH TALKS — ReElement Technologies and American Resources Target Africa's Premier REE Deposit
snippet: A consortium comprising Bunker Hill, ReElement Technologies and American Resources Corporation was selected by Kenya's Ministry of Mining on November 20 to enter exclusive negotiations for a prospecting licence at the Mrima Hill rare earth project — one of Africa's highest-grade and largest undeveloped niobium-rare earth carbonatite deposits, with historical resource estimates suggesting multi-decade production potential of heavy and light rare earth elements critical to magnets and EV motors. The selection follows a competitive government tender process and represents a significant North American-led bet on African rare earth supply development at a moment when US government policy is prioritizing domestic and allied-nation rare earth supply chains as a strategic counterweight to Chinese processing dominance.

headline: TRUMP PLEDGES TO 'CATCH CHINA' ON RARE EARTHS — Can Policy Rhetoric Save a Sector Down 40-50% in 2026?
snippet: 24/7 Wall St.'s November 19 analysis examines whether President Trump's pledge to "catch" China on rare earth production capacity — delivered amid escalating US-China trade tensions and bilateral talks that have so far failed to deliver a stable rare earth supply framework — can reverse the collapse of North American rare earth equity valuations, with USA Rare Earth (USAR) down more than 40% year-to-date and Critical Metals (CMET) down even further after a 28.7% single-week rout on Greenland acquisition dilution concerns. While USAR rose 5% and MP Materials gained 3% on the November 19 policy headlines, analysts note that Trump's rhetoric has previously sparked short-lived rallies in the sector without translating into the permitting reforms or government purchasing commitments that could structurally shift the investment thesis.

headline: AURA ENERGY TARGETS DECEMBER FID FOR MAURITANIA'S FIRST URANIUM MINE — $500M NPV BFS Complete; Nuclear Utility Offtake Deal Signed
snippet: Aura Energy (ASX: AEE; AIM: AURA) is targeting a final investment decision before year-end 2026 — with the December window now weeks away — following the October completion of its bankable feasibility study for the Tiris uranium project in Mauritania, which outlined a $500.3 million post-tax NPV on a 26-year operation with $349.8 million development capital, 83.7% uranium recovery, and a June 2026 non-binding MOU with a major nuclear utility covering potential investment and offtake at a base-case price of US$90/lb U3O8. A positive FID would trigger the first construction activities for what would be Mauritania's first uranium mine — in a year when uranium equities have been crushed by the same liquidity-crunch dynamics hitting other commodities, meaning a December FID would arrive at a moment of maximally negative investor sentiment and potentially provide one of the year's most contrarian development-stage catalysts.

headline: 'LIQUIDITY AND THE FED, NOT PEACE IN SHENZHEN' — Gold Loses a Third of Its Value as Geopolitical Headlines Can No Longer Save Metals
snippet: XTB's November 20 market analysis makes the case that gold's current collapse — now approximately 35% from its January 2026 all-time high above $5,500 per ounce — is structurally different from prior corrections because geopolitical risk premiums (US-China talks, Middle East, US-Russia) have been decoupled from the price by the dominant force of a rising US dollar and rising real Treasury yields acting in combination, creating a macro environment where every piece of geopolitical news that would historically be bullish for gold is immediately overwhelmed by the liquidity-tightening trade. The analysis notes that gold is now trading in correlation with equities rather than in opposition to them — moving down with risk assets on bad macro data rather than up as a haven — suggesting the corrective move has entered a phase driven by forced institutional liquidation rather than changes in the underlying supply-demand balance.

headline: 'THE BLACK FRIDAY GOLD CRASH' — November's $2,000 Drop From the Peak: Generational Setup or More Downside Ahead?
snippet: Macronomics' November 20 Substack analysis of the gold price rout argues that the confluence of forced liquidation, hawkish Fed positioning, and a broad risk-off sentiment shock has created a rare alignment of technical oversold conditions and structural supply-demand fundamentals that historically precedes multi-hundred-dollar recoveries — framing the November 2026 selloff as qualitatively similar to the 2008, 2013 and 2020 panic washouts that all subsequently resolved with strong recoveries once the liquidity event subsided. The piece distinguishes between the financial conditions driving the November 2026 selloff and the structural demand factors that remain intact (central bank net buying, de-dollarization, fiscal deficit monetization), and argues that investors with a 12-24 month horizon are being handed a rare entry at prices that reflect maximum institutional pessimism rather than fundamental deterioration.
